label: provisional
paradigm: These criteria serve a buyer choosing what to purchase, new or pre-owned: an evidence-based, value-aware buyer who wants an informed view of history and context. They are one reasonable buyer's stance, not the only one, and this version is provisional: drafted from published sources, not yet compiled or ratified.

change_log.reason: Drafted from menswear and dress-code guides (He Spoke Style, Gentleman's Gazette), a retailer's dress-watch guide (Watches of Switzerland), Deployant, Gear Patrol on fit, and the Teddy content audit of 2026-11-14. Every numeric threshold here is informed opinion, so the numeric criteria are classed contested.

spec_fields.case_mm: number: case diameter in millimetres, crown excluded
spec_fields.band: lower-case string describing the strap or bracelet, for example "black alligator leather strap"
spec_fields.complications: list of lower-case strings, for example "date", "chronograph", "gmt"; [] for time only

wearer.statement: Which dress codes the buyer must meet (black tie, suit, business casual) sets how strict the dress criteria are; a watch can be a dress watch and still be wrong with a tuxedo.
The watch fits the buyer's wrist: lug-to-lug length inside the flat top of the wrist and a thickness the buyer's cuffs and comfort allow. Measure these rather than trusting the stated diameter.
wearer.test: Compare the stated lug-to-lug length with the buyer's measured flat wrist width; try the watch on where possible.

watch.statement: Slim enough to slide under a shirt cuff. Thresholds differ: a retailer guide says less than 15 mm; Teddy reports buyers wanting Omega three-hand models under 12 mm. The rule uses 12 mm; a buyer can move it.
A modest case, 33 to 41 mm in one retailer's guide. Others hold that size should follow the wrist, not a fixed number.
A thin leather strap (black for black tie). Metal bracelets, rubber and nylon read as casual.
Time only, or a date window at most. Complications do not stop a watch being a dress watch but make it less formal.
A plain, legible dial without lume or busy decoration; white or silver is the purist's default.
A precious-metal case (gold is the classic black-tie match). Steel is acceptable but reads less formal.

principles_note: Teddy's principles are quoted from the videos' auto-captions (wording as captioned), located by text search of the caption track; timestamps are the caption segment where the quote begins. They enter as practitioner consensus, never as standards. His videos state his store is an authorized dealer for over 35 brands.
